name: Edom
overview: The name Edom primarily refers to Esau, identified by his red hair and the red stew for which he bargained (Genesis 25:25, 25:30). It also designates the land inhabited by Esau's descendants, extending from the Elanitic Gulf to the Red Sea, also called Idumea, with notable leaders such as the dukes descended from Eliphaz (Genesis 32:3, 36:1, 36:8, 36:16). Scripture presents Edom both as a historical people and territory, highlighting its origins and significance in relation to Israel.
